8.0.0.en: 1 In the third year of the reign of king Belshazzar a vision appeared unto me, even unto me Daniel, after that which appeared unto me at the first. 2 And I saw in a vision; and it came to pass, when I saw, that I was at Shushan in the palace, which is in the province of Elam; and I saw in a vision, and I was by the river of Ulai.

8.0.1.en: This vision took place a short time before the fall of Babylon, for the prophet Daniel saw himself as one who was in Shushan, the capital of the province of Elam, west of Persia, east of Babylon and south of Media.

8.0.2.en: "In the third year of the reign of king Belshazzar a vision appeared unto me, even unto me Daniel, after that which appeared unto me at the first" [1].

8.0.3.en: Daniel was granted by the Lord to stand as in a high watchtower, to see the distant things that no one else sees, which some may think illogical, and sometimes even impossible. This gift is offered to the faithful soul that throws itself into the bosom of God, who lifts it up as on the wings of a dove, to see even what lies beyond time.

8.0.4.en: This vision was granted to him two years after the previous vision, and shortly before the fall of Babylon (Dan 5). For this reason the vision passed over the Babylonian Empire and revealed the kingdom of Media and Persia (the ram), which is attacked by the kingdom of the Macedonians (the he-goat).

8.1.0.en: "And I saw in a vision; and it came to pass, when I saw, that I was at Shushan in the palace, which is in the province of Elam; and I saw in a vision, and I was by the river of Ulai" [2].

8.1.1.en: The city of Shushan, or Susa, is described in the Holy Bible as the citadel. It held a special position, since it was the capital of Persia; later, in the days of the Persian Empire, it came to share the status of capital with Babylon. It lies about 250 miles east of Babylon; one of them was used in winter and the other in summer, and it became the capital of Cyrus. Daniel was in the palace in Babylon, but in the vision he saw himself as though he were by the river of Ulai. Some thought that Daniel was in the city of Shushan, but this is not acceptable, for it was not possible for Daniel the captive to leave Babylon and dwell in Shushan, which belonged to Persia; rather he saw himself thus in the vision. Perhaps God permitted this to reassure him that, as he had served his people during the Babylonian rule, he would serve them also during the Persian rule. Most probably the palace of Shushan had not yet been built, because the Persian Empire had not yet flourished.

8.2.0.en: 3 Then I lifted up mine eyes, and saw, and, behold, there stood before the river a ram which had two horns: and the two horns were high; but one was higher than the other, and the higher came up last. 4 I saw the ram pushing westward, and northward, and southward; so that no beasts might stand before him, neither was there any that could deliver out of his hand; but he did according to his will, and became great.

8.2.1.en: In the previous vision Daniel saw four beasts, but here he sees two animals, the first being a ram with two horns.

8.2.2.en: As the time of Babylon's collapse before Persia and Media drew near, Daniel saw this vision. He saw a ram standing by the river, having two high horns, one higher than the other. St. Hippolytus of Rome says: [By this ram, pushing westward, northward and southward, he means Darius, king of the Persians, who overcame all the nations, as it is said, "no beasts might stand before him".]

8.2.3.en: "Then I lifted up mine eyes, and saw, and, behold, there stood before the river a ram which had two horns: and the two horns were high; but one was higher than the other, and the higher came up last.

8.2.4.en: I saw the ram pushing westward, and northward, and southward; so that no beasts might stand before him, neither was there any that could deliver out of his hand; but he did according to his will, and became great" [3-4].

8.2.5.en: When the prophet Daniel felt that he was called to see divine mysteries of the future, he lifted up his eyes to see. It is as though the vision, although it appears to concern the emergence of the kingdoms of Persia, Media and Greece, in its essence touches the eternity of the believers and their enjoyment of what is above time. Thus it is not for us to ignore chronological history, but when the Spirit of God lifts up our eyes we see God's hidden plan, which works through history to carry us beyond history.

8.2.6.en: With wonderful precision the kingdom of Persia was likened to the ram with two horns, one higher than the other, because Persia became greater than Media. Cyrus the Persian married the daughter of his maternal uncle Cyaxares (Darius the Mede). Darius was very weak in character compared with Cyrus, who far surpassed his father-in-law; nevertheless he left him as a partner with him in the rule, and so the prophecy was fulfilled literally.

8.2.7.en: Here the two horns correspond to the two sides of the second beast (the bear) in the previous vision, where it raised itself up on one side (Dan 7:5), and also to the two shoulders of the great metal image, the Colossus, in Nebuchadnezzar's dream mentioned in the second chapter. The pushing of the ram signifies the swift victories achieved by the Persians.

8.2.8.en: Since Persia was likened to the ram, the other kings were likened to the beasts, which could not stand before him, nor escape from his hands.

8.2.9.en: Marcellinus says: [When the king of the Persians was at the head of his army, he wore the head of a ram on his head instead of the crown.]

8.3.0.en: 5 And as I was considering, behold, an he goat came from the west on the face of the whole earth, and touched not the ground: and the goat had a notable horn between his eyes. 6 And he came to the ram that had two horns, which I had seen standing before the river, and ran unto him in the fury of his power. 7 And I saw him come close unto the ram, and he was moved with choler against him, and smote the ram, and brake his two horns: and there was no power in the ram to stand before him, but he cast him down to the ground, and stamped upon him: and there was none that could deliver the ram out of his hand. 8 Therefore the he goat waxed very great: and when he was strong, the great horn was broken; and for it came up four notable ones toward the four winds of heaven.

8.3.1.en: "And as I was considering, behold, an he goat came from the west on the face of the whole earth, and touched not the ground: and the goat had a notable horn between his eyes.

8.3.2.en: And he came to the ram that had two horns, which I had seen standing before the river, and ran unto him in the fury of his power" [5-6].

8.3.3.en: When the ram appeared with power and authority, pushing every beast it met, an enemy appeared to it: a he-goat with a notable horn between his eyes. The prophet saw him coming from the west, where Greece lies, west of Persia. The goat was so swift that his feet did not touch the ground [5]. With his army he was more like a bird flying in the air than one coming over land or by the fleet at sea. Persia was likened to the ram in comparison with the Greek kingdom, which was likened to the he-goat. For the goat is more agile and swifter in movement than the ram. So Alexander the Great was swifter in his movements.

8.4.0.en: He smote the ram, and brake his two horns, and cast him down to the ground, and stamped upon him, and there was none that could deliver the ram out of his hand [7].

8.4.1.en: "And I saw him come close unto the ram, and he was moved with choler against him, and smote the ram, and brake his two horns: and there was no power in the ram to stand before him, but he cast him down to the ground, and stamped upon him: and there was none that could deliver the ram out of his hand" [7].

8.4.2.en: This is a true vision that was fulfilled more than 200 years later. Here God shows His prophet the victory of Alexander, who subdued the whole East, entering into many battles; but the vision focuses on Persia, which dominated many nations, and which was previously likened to the ram that pushes in every direction of the world.

8.4.3.en: He saw the goat come to the ram, a thing that no one expected, since the great cities were fortified, and the distance between Persia and Greece was great. But Alexander reached Persia and defeated it with unexpected power and speed. Darius was defeated in two dramatic battles. He was defeated in the first battle and tried to gather his forces again, and indeed he entered with him into a second battle, but his followers betrayed him, and the battle ended with his being killed by them.

8.4.4.en: Some historians say that Alexander claimed to be the son of the god Jupiter Ammon, who was symbolized in the form of a goat, and historical pictures have been discovered depicting a goat with a single horn as a symbol of the ancient Greek armies.

8.5.0.en: "Therefore the he goat waxed very great: and when he was strong, the great horn was broken; and for it came up four notable ones toward the four winds of heaven" [8].

8.5.1.en: St. Hippolytus of Rome says: [By the he-goat coming from the west he means Alexander the Macedonian, coming from Greece... Alexander stirred up war against Darius and overcame him, and established himself as lord over the whole kingdom after he had defeated him with a shameful defeat and destroyed his camp. After the goat was glorified, his great horn was broken, and four horns came up under it toward the four winds of heaven. For when Alexander had established himself as lord over all the land of the Persians and subdued its people, he died, and his kingdom was divided among four rulers.]

8.5.2.en: The goat waxed very great, and at the height of his greatness a wonderful change occurred: the notable horn was broken, and in its place came up four notable ones, extending toward the four winds of heaven [8]. At the death of Alexander the Great, his kingdom was divided among his four generals into four kingdoms: Macedonia, Thrace, Syria and Egypt. None of them was equal to him in strength. Historians differ concerning his death; some think he died of sickness, and others think he died poisoned. Before his death he was asked who should succeed him; in his pride he saw no one worthy to succeed him, and he said: "The man who counts himself most worthy of this empire!" He had two sons, one of them by Roxana, the daughter of Darius, and he also had a brother called Aridaeus, but he saw none of them worthy to succeed him, as though there were no one in the whole world like him. When he became unable to speak, he took the ring from his hand and gave it to Perdiccas. After his death there were many disturbances and about 15 generals were killed.

8.5.3.en: Cassander, the son of Antipater, became king over Macedonia after killing Olympias, the mother of Alexander, and his sister, his son, his wife Roxana, and many of his relatives. The generals lost confidence in one another, and each general feared his colleagues, for a spirit of treachery and betrayal prevailed among them. Finally, 15 years after his death, the kingdom was divided into four parts, which are:

8.5.4.en: A. Macedonia, over which Cassander the son of Antipater reigned, and to which were joined some parts of Thrace together with the cities of Greece.

8.5.5.en: B. Syria, Babylonia and all the kingdoms of the East, over which Seleucus Nicanor reigned.

8.5.6.en: C. Asia Minor, over which Antigonus reigned, annexing Phrygia, Paphlagonia and the other Asian regions, after killing 5 or 6 of the generals.

8.5.7.en: D. Egypt, over which Ptolemy the son of Lagos reigned.

8.5.8.en: These are the four notable horns [8] that ruled the world in the East, the West, the North and the South.

8.6.0.en: 9 And out of one of them came forth a little horn, which waxed exceeding great, toward the south, and toward the east, and toward the pleasant land. 10 And it waxed great, even to the host of heaven; and it cast down some of the host and of the stars to the ground, and stamped upon them. 11 Yea, he magnified himself even to the prince of the host, and by him the daily sacrifice was taken away, and the place of his sanctuary was cast down. 12 And an host was given him against the daily sacrifice by reason of transgression, and it cast down the truth to the ground; and it practised, and prospered. 13 Then I heard one saint speaking, and another saint said unto that certain saint which spake,

8.6.1.en: "How long shall be the vision concerning the daily sacrifice, and the transgression of desolation, to give both the sanctuary and the host to be trodden under foot?" 14 And he said unto me, "Unto two thousand and three hundred days; then shall the sanctuary be cleansed." [9-14].

8.7.0.en: What is this little horn but the antichrist of the Old Testament, Antiochus Epiphanes, who also symbolizes the Antichrist at the end of the ages? He was called the little horn, not by comparison with the rest of the kings of his time, but because no one expected him to take the throne after his father; yet he seized the rule by his cunning and craftiness. Epiphanes reigned over Syria (the northern kingdom of the Greek Empire) about the year 175 BC. The prophet Daniel spoke of him in more detail in (Dan 11:21-35). He was called the most defiled man of the Old Testament, and he persecuted the Jews. After the death of his brother he met the people and pretended great kindness and deceived them, so they made him king; and he slaughtered a swine and sprinkled its blood on the altar and the holy vessels, and forbade the offering of the daily sacrifices [11], on pain of death.

8.7.1.en: * Antiochus, called Epiphanes, arose from the line of Alexander, and when he reigned over Syria and subdued Egypt under his authority, he went up to Jerusalem, entered the Temple, and seized all the treasures of the house of the Lord, the golden lampstand, the table and the altar, and made a great slaughter in the land, as it is written: "The sanctuary shall be trodden under foot for one thousand three hundred evenings and mornings." It came to pass that the sanctuary remained desolate all this time - three and a half years - so the one thousand three hundred days were fulfilled. Then Judas Maccabeus appeared after the death of his father Mattathias and resisted him, and destroyed the camp of Antiochus, and delivered the city, and cleansed the sanctuary and restored it carefully, as ordained in the Law.

8.7.2.en: This was clearly described in the books of the Maccabees.

8.7.3.en: St. Hippolytus of Rome: "Waxed great toward the south" [9], that is, toward Egypt, for he wanted to seize Egypt, but the Senate sent Pompilius to him to make him leave Egypt, and in his deceitful way he asked the messenger for a delay in order to leave Egypt; but the messenger, holding a staff, drew a circle on the ground around him and said: "Before you go out of this circle, give me an answer, and do not deceive me by saying that you are seeking the counsel of advisers." So he was compelled to leave Egypt. But afterwards he entered into war against Ptolemy Philopator, king of Egypt.

8.7.4.en: He turned toward the east [9], for his kingdom extended as far as Ptolemais, and he fought those who rebelled against him in Persia.

8.7.5.en: Then toward "the pleasant land" [9], that is, the glorious lands, or the land of promise, "Canaan". As it is said in Jeremiah, "And give thee a pleasant land, a goodly heritage of the hosts of nations" (Jer 3:19); "And hast given them this land, which thou didst swear to their fathers to give them, a land flowing with milk and honey" (Jer 31:22). It was also called the pleasant land because of the presence of the glorious Temple of the Lord in Judah, and Antiochus fought the Jews and defiled their Temple.

8.7.6.en: Antiochus (or the Antichrist) waxes great even to the host of heaven and casts down some of the host and of the stars to the ground [10]. Thus God declares to His prophet Daniel concerning His Church that she is heaven, and that the believers are the host of Christ and her stars.

8.7.7.en: And as Antiochus opposed the believers - the Church of the Old Testament - and killed many, so the Antichrist will exert all his effort to destroy the stars of the New Testament. For this reason the Lord Christ says concerning His final coming: "When the Son of man cometh, shall he find faith on the earth?" As He also says concerning the Antichrist: "if it were possible, they shall deceive the very elect."

8.7.8.en: The matter does not stop at the stars of heaven or its host, but the enemy magnifies himself against the prince of the host [11], that is, the Jewish high priest whom Antiochus Epiphanes persecuted. St. Jerome thinks that by the prince of the host he means God Himself, the Lord of hosts, for Antiochus stood against Him, and did not leave any part of the Temple holy for the worship of the living God, but defiled the whole Temple and its annexes. And since he forbade the offering of the daily sacrifice endelekhismos, the temple of the Lord became as though it did not exist. St. Jerome says that Antiochus did this not because of his courage but because of the sins of the people. All this bears a symbol of what the Antichrist, who sets himself up as God, will do.

8.8.0.en: And the matter does not stop at opposing the worship of God, but extends to corrupting the divine teachings, for it says of him that "it cast down the truth to the ground" [12]. Thus the vision links worship with sound doctrine. On the other hand, the enemy of good can cast down the truth to the ground, but he cannot snatch it away from heaven. It is as though whoever lives in the heavenly realms carries within him, alongside spiritual worship, the truth itself.

8.8.1.en: When Daniel's heart was lifted up to heaven, he saw an angel (a saint) asking another angel, although some think that he was asking the Word of God: "How long shall be the vision concerning the daily sacrifice...?" The angels do not know all the mysteries (Eph 3:10), but in their love for mankind and their longing for the perfection of their glory they inquire about what concerns the Church, and perhaps they feared that the period of tribulation would be prolonged, so that the believers would lose their faith and their crowns.

8.9.s.en: Scholars differed concerning this little horn:

8.9.0.en: A. Some think that it is the very same little horn mentioned in chapter 7.

8.9.1.en: B. Others distinguish between the two, holding that the little horn mentioned in chapter 7 refers to the Antichrist, while the one mentioned here refers to Antiochus Epiphanes, whom some regard as the "antichrist" of the Old Testament period.

8.9.2.en: C. There is an opinion that reconciles the two previous opinions, namely that what is mentioned here in chapter eight refers to Antiochus, who in turn refers to the Antichrist; as though what is mentioned in chapter seven refers to the Antichrist directly, while this chapter refers to him indirectly.

8.9.3.en: As for the period concerning the vindication or cleansing of the sanctuary, which is 2300 evenings and mornings: lest the day here be understood as a symbol of a year, it says "evenings and mornings", which means 2300 real days. St. Jerome thinks that it equals 6 years and three months, and that it represents the period from the beginning of Antiochus' opposition to worship until Judas Maccabeus triumphed over him. St. Hippolytus of Rome, on the other hand, thinks that 2300 evenings and mornings means 1150 days (2300÷2), since the two daily sacrifices (the morning and the evening) were forbidden during the persecution, and this equals about three and a half years, for Judas Maccabeus cleansed the Temple after it had been defiled by Antiochus.

8.9.4.en: Many commentators think that 2300 evenings and mornings affirms that they are real days, and that they equal 6 years, 4 months and 20 prophetic days, since the year in the Holy Bible equals 360 prophetic days and the month 30 days. This is the actual period that begins on 5 August 71 BC, that is, from the beginning of the transgression of desolation, when Jason was appointed high priest through intrigues, and pledged to the king that he would pay him 260 talents of silver if he would permit him to establish a place to teach the young men of the Jews the customs of the pagans and to call them Antiochenes, and he permitted him to do so. And indeed he introduced the customs of the pagans among his people, and they adopted their dress and wore their hats, and the priests despised the Temple of God and its sacrifices and were busy with the Greek games, preferring them above everything. As it is said in the book of the Maccabees: "In those days there went out of Israel wicked men, and persuaded many, saying: Let us go and make a covenant with the nations that are round about us: for since we departed from them we have found much evil; and the saying seemed good in their eyes... and they forsook the holy covenant, and joined themselves to the nations, and were sold to do mischief" (1 Macc 1:11-15). If Daniel's prophecy is reckoned from this event until the restoration of worship to its origin and the cleansing of the sanctuary on 25 December 165, the period is exactly 2300 days. In other words, what is mentioned here includes the period in which all the calamities befell the Temple in the days of Antiochus Epiphanes, from the first transgression of desolation to the end of the period of the abolition of the daily sacrifice, when Judas Maccabeus delivered the Jews from Antiochus.

8.9.5.en: The painful events that Jerusalem suffered at that time are:

8.9.6.en: A. The appointment of Jason as high priest and his sharing with Antiochus in the pagan abominations.

8.9.7.en: B. The attack of Antiochus on Jerusalem, his entering the Temple and plundering its treasures, and the offering of a swine on the altar (1 Kgs 1:20-28).

8.9.8.en: C. Two years later, when the false report of his death spread and the Jews rejoiced, he sent to them Apollonius, one of his commanders, who dealt cruelly with the city, then burned it, razed its walls, and built from its ruins a strong fortress on a mountain overlooking the Temple (1 Macc 2:29; 2 Macc 5:11-14).

8.9.9.en: D. He officially forbade the offering of burnt offerings and sacrifices in the Temple (1 Macc 1:54), and that was in the month of June 197 BC.

8.9.10.en: Concerning what befell the Jews at the hands of Antiochus Epiphanes, we distinguish two main periods:

8.9.11.en: A. A period of 2300 days that includes all the previous events, beginning with Jason's appointment as high priest and ending with the victory of Judas Maccabeus.

8.9.12.en: B. A period of 1290 days, or about three and a half years, beginning with the removal of the daily sacrifice, the setting up of the statue of Jupiter in the Temple, and the defiling of the sanctuary after Antiochus took possession of Jerusalem by means of his commander Apollonius.

8.10.0.en: 15 And it came to pass, when I, even I Daniel, had seen the vision, and sought for the meaning, then, behold, there stood before me as the appearance of a man. 16 And I heard a man's voice between the banks of Ulai, which called, and said, "Gabriel, make this man to understand the vision." 17 So he came near where I stood: and when he came, I was afraid, and fell upon my face: but he said unto me, "Understand, O son of man: for at the time of the end shall be the vision." 18 Now as he was speaking with me, I was in a deep sleep on my face toward the ground: but he touched me, and set me upright. 19 And he said, "Behold, I will make thee know what shall be in the last end of the indignation: for at the time appointed the end shall be. 20 The ram which thou sawest having two horns are the kings of Media and Persia. 21 And the rough goat is the king of Grecia: and the great horn that is between his eyes is the first king. 22 Now that being broken, whereas four stood up for it, four kingdoms shall stand up out of the nation, but not in his power. 23 And in the latter time of their kingdom, when the transgressors are come to the full, a king of fierce countenance, and understanding dark sentences, shall stand up. 24 And his power shall be mighty, but not by his own power: and he shall destroy wonderfully, and shall prosper, and practise, and shall destroy the mighty and the holy people. 25 And through his policy also he shall cause craft to prosper in his hand; and he shall magnify himself in his heart, and by peace shall destroy many: he shall also stand up against the Prince of princes; but he shall be broken without hand. 26 And the vision of the evening and the morning which was told is true: wherefore shut thou up the vision; for it shall be for many days." 27 And I Daniel fainted, and was sick certain days; afterward I rose up, and did the king's business; and I was astonished at the vision, but none understood it.

8.10.1.en: "And it came to pass, when I, even I Daniel, had seen the vision, and sought for the meaning, then, behold, there stood before me as the appearance of a man.

8.10.2.en: And I heard a man's voice between the banks of Ulai, which called, and said,

8.10.3.en: Gabriel, make this man to understand the vision" [15-16].

8.10.4.en: The prophet Daniel desired a fuller interpretation of the vision, for he knew little; but for his own benefit and for the benefit of the Church as a whole he desired to search for the meaning, and before he asked he saw "the appearance of a man" [15]; most probably the Word of God before the Incarnation, who has authority to command the archangel Gabriel to interpret the vision for him [16]. It is as though God, who knows the secrets of the heart, when He sees the inner man longing for the truth, grants it to him in abundance, and asks His heavenly servants to reveal to him some of the hidden mysteries.

8.10.5.en: "So he came near where I stood: and when he came, I was afraid, and fell upon my face:

8.10.6.en: but he said unto me, Understand, O son of man:

8.10.7.en: for at the time of the end shall be the vision.

8.10.8.en: Now as he was speaking with me, I was prostrate (in a deep sleep) on my face toward the ground: but he touched me, and set me upright.

8.10.9.en: And he said, Behold, I will make thee know what shall be in the last end of the indignation:

8.11.0.en: for at the time appointed the end shall be" [17-19].

8.11.1.en: St. Jerome justifies the calling of Daniel "son of man" by saying: [Since Ezekiel, Daniel and Zechariah saw that they were often in the company of angels, they were always reminded of their weakness, lest they be lifted up with pride and think that they shared in the nature or dignity of the angels. Therefore they were called sons of men (sons of Adam), that they might realize that they were nothing but human beings.]

8.11.2.en: When the archangel drew near to Daniel, the prophet fell in terror. Perhaps Daniel discovered the gravity of the vision, and God's concern to reveal its mysteries to him by means of an archangel, so he received this interpretation in fear and reverence. He recorded this for us so that we should not make light of the vision or treat its interpretation with contempt, but that our minds, like our lives, must be prepared to know it with diligence and seriousness. The angel made clear to him that this vision is "at the time of the end" [17], that is, it concerns the future. Here perhaps he means its fulfillment in the days of Antiochus and, even more, shortly before the last coming of Christ. He affirms that the vision will surely and fully be fulfilled, but at the appropriate time appointed for it.

8.11.3.en: The archangel raised him from his deep sleep, that his mind might be kindled with knowledge, and he comforted him, and also assured him of the destruction of this little horn. It is said that Antiochus died an evil death, as worms ate his body, like Herod Agrippa I (Acts 12). So also the Antichrist will be struck, and his kingdom will perish.

8.11.4.en: "The ram which thou sawest having two horns are the kings of Media and Persia.

8.11.5.en: And the rough goat is the king of Grecia: and the great horn that is between his eyes is the first king.

8.11.6.en: Now that being broken, whereas four stood up for it, four kingdoms shall stand up out of the nation, but not in his power.

8.11.7.en: And in the latter time of their kingdom, when the transgressors are come to the full, a king of fierce countenance, and understanding dark sentences, shall stand up.

8.11.8.en: And his power shall be mighty, but not by his own power:

8.11.9.en: and he shall destroy wonderfully, and shall prosper, and practise, and shall destroy the mighty and the holy people.

8.12.0.en: And through his policy also he shall cause craft to prosper in his hand; and he shall magnify himself in his heart, and by peace shall destroy many: he shall also stand up against the Prince of princes; but he shall be broken without hand" [22-25].

8.12.1.en: We have already explained what is stated in the previous phrases. Here the archangel affirms to Daniel the meaning of the ram and the he-goat, removing the least doubt concerning their interpretation.

8.12.2.en: Here he calls Antiochus a king of fierce countenance, that is, a king with a hard, unyielding face, and he also calls him one who understands dark sentences or riddles, because he was skilled in deception.

8.13.0.en: The prophet Daniel prophesied concerning Antiochus, saying that by peace or security he shall destroy many [25], and this was fulfilled when he sent his commander with 22,000 men to Jerusalem as a mission of peace. These soldiers would go in and out until the Jews felt secure with them, and the men treated the people with great kindness, so that they did not suspect them. And on the Sabbath, while the Jews were worshiping in the Temple, orders were given to kill them all, and thousands were killed, and thus by security he destroyed many.

8.13.1.en: The prophet Daniel also prophesied his standing up against the Prince of princes and his being broken without human hand [25], and this was accomplished when Antiochus Epiphanes opposed God Himself, the Prince of princes and King of kings. And he remained so for more than 6 years (2300 days). The Maccabees resisted him, and by their hands the Temple was cleansed and victory over him was achieved. He heard that the Jews under the leadership of the Maccabees had removed the statue of Jupiter Olympius from the Temple, which he himself had placed there, so he was greatly enraged and gathered a huge army and decided to exterminate the Jewish race completely, but he was struck with a very sharp pain in his bowels, and died at once from the intensity of the pain, and thus he perished by divine permission without the use of a human hand.

8.13.2.en: "And the vision of the evening and the morning which was told is true:

8.13.3.en: wherefore shut thou up (seal) the vision; for it shall be for many days.

8.13.4.en: And I Daniel fainted, and was sick certain days; afterward I rose up, and did the king's business;

8.14.0.en: and I was astonished at the vision, but none understood it" [26-27].

8.14.1.en: By saying: "the vision of the evening and the morning which was told is true" [26], he means that the vision is true in its dark aspect, where there is severe tribulation, and its bright aspect, where God declares the victory of His people.

8.14.2.en: Daniel could not bear the vision, so he became sick, unable to leave his bed, for some days. But he was terrified of what would befall the Church, whether in the days of Antiochus or of the Antichrist. Yet, as St. Jerome says: [He rose up to do the king's business, rendering unto Caesar the things which be Caesar's, and unto God the things which be God's (Lk 20:25).

8.15.0.en: In any case Daniel did not grasp all the mysteries of the vision, and the future unsealing of them with the passing of the times, for he says: "I was astonished at the vision, but none understood it" [27].

8.16.s.en: The four empires in the book of Daniel

8.16.0.en: Daniel 2 Daniel 7 Daniel 8 The head of gold Winged lion Babylonian 626 BC.

8.16.1.en: Chest and arms of silver Bear Ram Media and Persia 539 BC.

8.16.2.en: Belly and thighs of bronze Leopard He-goat Greek [including the Ptolemies and the Seleucids].

8.16.4.en: Legs of iron Terrifying beast Roman 63 BC.

8.16.5.en: And feet of clay Unlike any other Fall of Jerusalem 70 BC.

8.17.s.en: I became perplexed and did not understand!

8.17.0.en: * The archangel Gabriel accompanied Your prophet Daniel and gave him an interpretation of some of Your mysteries, and here he cries out after his body was loosed in weakness:

8.17.1.en: I was astonished at the vision, and did not understand!

8.17.2.en: * Reveal to me the mysteries of Your love, that I may see all history in the grasp of Your hands, and see my whole life as the object of Your care!

8.17.3.en: Grant me the company of Your angels, but remind me of my weakness lest I exalt myself.

8.17.4.en: Remember that I am a weak son of Adam.

8.17.5.en: In You I become strong and wise!

8.17.6.en: * Let the powerful kingdoms succeed one another, and let the Antichrist appear, for You alone are the fortress of the Church and her strength!

8.17.7.en: You will not allow him to reign except for a limited time!

8.17.8.en: His kingdom will end, and Your saints will reign in heaven forever!
